summary: The base failure was reproduced and the exact candidate fixes the FP32 output contract on the assigned ROCm gfx950 GPU. The registered aten::mm.dtype path, actual deterministic MoEGate branch, near-tied routing, FP64-reference accuracy, repeated execution, sub-batch invariance, tile-boundary shapes, bias, and token-count boundaries all passed. CUDA and real DeepGEMM execution remain architecture-unverified.

tests.what_was_measured: Reproduced BF16-rounded values in a nominal FP32 aten::mm.dtype result: 0/4352 non-BF16 values, 0.966156 max error versus CPU FP64, and collapsed near-tied expert scores.
Direct FP32 retention in 4351/4352 values, 0.000305176 max error versus CPU FP64, correct near-tied expert winner, and exact repeat/sub-batch invariance.
Candidate regression suite: 11 passed and 54 subtests passed.
Independent tile-boundary shapes, FP32 bias, repeated outputs, and actual deterministic gate prefix invariance across 1/4/5/16/17 tokens.

gpu_execution_evidence: All numerical probes and regressions ran on AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2/HIP 7.2.
remaining_counterexamples: No failing counterexample was found on ROCm gfx950.
CUDA kernel execution is unverified because no NVIDIA GPU was assigned.
Actual DeepGEMM execution is unverified because DeepGEMM is unavailable on this AMD host; only the intentional FP32 bypass was source-reviewed and mock-tested.
remaining_limitations: The review cannot honestly claim universal full resolution without executing the CUDA specialization on supported NVIDIA hardware.
No native rebuild was performed because the candidate contains no native C++ or FlyDSL changes.
The tiny Llama serving fixture is not relevant evidence for DeepSeek router numerical semantics and was not run.
